conventions.convention: The one-dimensional carrier is the complex space ℋ₁ = L²(R,dx) of almost-everywhere classes, with inner product linear in its first argument. H₁ denotes the energy operator, not the Hilbert space.

m, ω and ℏ are positive; ℓ = sqrt(ℏ/(mω)). Position is the maximal multiplication operator Qf = xf, and momentum is Pf = −iℏDₓf on the classes with an L² weak derivative. Their assigned units are metres and kg m s⁻¹.

The energy operator is fixed by unitary scaling of the diagonal Hermite operator. Its differential expression holds pointwise on the polynomial-Gaussian core and weakly on its domain; no independently defined maximal differential domain is identified with that domain.

V(0) is subtracted as a potential-energy offset. Energy coordinates are in joules; the resulting one-dimensional ground energy is ℏω/2. Nψ is dimensionless with declared unit 1/count. The one-dimensional and isotropic three-dimensional realizations are separately adopted models.
The coherent series starts at n = 0. Its label z is dimensionless; z = 0 has no phase label and gives the ground vector. Preparations are rays, so a common phase does not change a preparation.
The Poisson weights are e^(−s)sⁿ/n! for s = |z|², with s⁰ = 1 also when s = 0. Initial means x₀ and p₀ are defined for every complex label, including zero.

The model adopts P1, P2, P4 and P5 and assumes Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Its predictions are conditional model conclusions; laboratory identifications and measured inputs are not supplied.

load_bearing.statement: Under P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the stated choice assumptions, fixes positive parameters m, ω, ℏ, the one-dimensional assigned Q, P, H₁ and Nψ with their exact domains and units, and the separate isotropic three-dimensional H₃. H₁ is the scaled diagonal Hermite operator; its flow is exp(−itH₁/ℏ). The quadratic potential and observable assignments are adopted model assumptions with no empirical identification.

For the adopted oscillator model and stated choice assumptions, σ(H₁) = {ℏω(n+1/2): n ∈ N}, ker(H₁−EₙI) = Cψₙ, D(H₁) = D(Nψ), and H₁ = ℏω(Nψ+I/2). The statement calls the complete orthonormal family (ψₙ) itself a core for H₁. For every unit f ∈ ℋ₁, μ_f(B) = Σ_{Eₙ∈B}|⟨f,ψₙ⟩|². The three-dimensional isotropic energies are ℏω(M+3/2) with multiplicities (M+1)(M+2)/2.

For each z ∈ C, Ψ_z = exp(−|z|²/2) Σ_{n=0}∞ zⁿψₙ/sqrt(n!) is a unit vector in every polynomial number domain, satisfies aψΨ_z = zΨ_z, and has overlap ⟨Ψ_z,Ψ_w⟩ = exp(−(|z|²+|w|²)/2+z conjugate(w)). Distinct labels define distinct preparations; Ψ₀ = ψ₀.

Every coherent vector lies in D(Q) ∩ D(P) and has spreads ℓ/sqrt(2) and ℏ/(ℓsqrt(2)), with product ℏ/2. Every unit f ∈ D(Q) ∩ D(P) satisfies Δ_fQ Δ_fP ≥ ℏ/2. For every coherent label, the centered pairing is −iℏ/2 and the centered vectors are linearly dependent.

For every complex label z and real time t, U(t)Ψ_z = exp(−iωt/2)Ψ_{z exp(−iωt)}. The preparation means obey x(t) = x₀cos(ωt)+p₀sin(ωt)/(mω) and p(t) = p₀cos(ωt)−mωx₀sin(ωt), with constant position and momentum spreads. The energy law is the affine pushforward of Poisson(|z|²), has mean ℏω(|z|²+1/2), and spread ℏω|z|.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. If U:H→K is a bijective linear inner-product-preserving map and T is self-adjoint with spectral PVM E_T, then T′ on UD(T), defined by T′Ux = UTx, is self-adjoint; E_{T′}(B) = UE_T(B)U⁻¹ is its regular spectral PVM; scalar laws agree for corresponding unit vectors; and σ(T′) = σ(T).

concerns.concern: Statement (a) says 'the family (ψₙ) is a complete orthonormal family of ℋ₁ and a core for H₁'; proof step 2.1 repeats that the family is a core. This is false literally. The published core definition requires a graph-norm-dense linear subspace, whereas the basis family is neither a linear subspace nor norm-dense. For u = (ψ₀+ψ₁)/sqrt(2), its squared distance from every basis vector is at least 2−sqrt(2)>0. The scaling supplier, clause (c), proves that the algebraic span of the family is a core; Facts F2 and step 1.1 correctly retain that span.

The 'Status of the mathematics' paragraph calls the context 'the published framework and spectral items cited in each item's contract'. The opened framework carriers, including post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition and def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units, have status: draft, as do the framework observable and evolution definitions. Distinguish current-run draft framework suppliers from published mathematical spectral suppliers.

seams_checked.note: The Robertson bound retains its product-domain hypothesis. The extension to D(Q) ∩ D(P) uses the separately cited graph approximation, rather than asserting unbounded products there.

The domains, spectrum, coherent formulas and multidimensional multiplicities agree, but the energy theorem's Statement (a) and step 2.1 strengthen the scaling supplier's 'span ... is a core' to the basis family itself being a core. See the owning concern.
This is a declared reading-order prerequisite. No assigned item's deduction invokes a Fock or equilibrium proposition, and no photon or thermal interpretation is imported.
The postulates remain adopted assumptions, units and dimensions agree, and the model introduces its unbounded quadratic potential separately from P5's bounded baseline.
Coherent preparations are unit rays. Distinctness uses overlap modulus, and global phase is excluded from the physical preparation.
Assigned observables carry domains and units. Atomic energy laws use eigenspace projections and countable additivity; moments retain domain membership.
The adopted flow is exp(−itH₁/ℏ), with the correct sign and generator domain. The explicit diagonal group is identified with that flow.
The maximal Q and P domains and Fourier normalization agree. The one-dimensional line model is explicitly an additional adoption; the three-dimensional model uses the spinless specialization.
The examples retain dimensioned parameters and declared units and assert no measurements or laboratory identifications.
The Gaussian laws use multiplication PVMs and Fourier transport. Ladder norms are distinguished from observable outcomes.
Spreads are outcome-law standard deviations, and saturation concerns separately assigned Q and P laws, without a joint sharp law or apparatus-error claim.
The ground representative, scaled eigenvalues and finite ladder actions preserve the mathematical suppliers' parameters and normalization.
Momentum uses the 2π Fourier convention and p = 2πℏξ; the resulting density has the correct Jacobian.
Reading-order context only; no Fock-space or equilibrium result is used or strengthened in the assigned examples.
Permutation-invariance Facts F3 uses the general unitary spectral-transport lemma with domain UD(T), without importing the physical oscillator assumptions.
The inspected page and its item references use this as reading-order context; no oscillator proposition is cited as an approximation guarantee.
The common-domain theorem retains the oscillator's energy and position assignments and adds H(t) = Hosc−f(t)Q as a further model assumption, with its own self-adjointness and propagator suppliers.
The driven-response example's L2 faithfully quotes free coherent rotation, means and spreads. Its forced response is obtained from a separate displacement-propagator supplier.
